newsitem.title: INDIA: India call edge up, new govt bond sold at discount.
newsitem.headline: India call edge up, new govt bond sold at discount.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday in the 10.25-10.50 range, marginally up from Tuesday's closing level of 10.0-10.5 percent, dealers said.
They said most of the deals were at 10.50 percent. Some deals were also reported at 10.75 percent.

"Some repo transactions were struck directly with Reserve Bank of India (RBI) at 10.75 percent to 11 percent against securities, which kept call range-bound between 10.0 percent and 10.75 percent", one bank dealer added.
The securities market saw trades in 13.50 percent 1997 at 13.24 percent, 12 percent 1999 at 13.63 percent and zero coupon bond maturing in 1999 at 14.14 percent, dealers said.

The latest auctioned 13.82 percent 2002 was traded at 13.92 percent, which is 10 basis points above the auctioned yield, a dealer said. "Primary Dealers (PDs) have offloaded their securities at discounted price ranging from Rs.99.68 to Rs.99.80."
The trasury bill maturing in January were traded at 11.65 and 11.70, a dealer said. The certificates of deposit (CDs) and commercial paper (CPs) markets were inactive, dealers said.
The intercorporate deposit rates were unchanged at 17-19 percent range, a dealer said.
